The shock winds you and [character]’s hands wrap around your throat before you have a chance to react. Moments separate you from death.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Intercessional Suspicion

options.text: We must keep our friends like [character] close.

events.text: You meet alone in your rooms. [character]’s eyes dart around as he enters. “Well met [character]! I have a message from [character]…” [character] takes half a step forwards and then stops, eyes bulging and a confused look upon his face. [character] pulls the dagger out of [character]’s back. “You’re safe now, my [title].” Was there really a plot on your life? A search of [character]’s body offers no clues and the dead tell no tales.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Intercessional Suspicion
events.text: You meet alone in your rooms. [character]’s eyes dart around as he enters. “Well met [character]! I have a message from [character]…” [character] takes half a step forwards. “He is happy to support you and wanted me to give you this personal donation for the [rival] coffers.” [character] places the valuable jewels on the table for you and thanks you again before leaving. You think of the suspicions that [character] placed in your mind. Will you praise or punish your Spymaster’s actions?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Investigation of a Tragedy

options.text: Thank you for the report. I never knew how disturbed he was.

events.text: After investigating, it appears that [character] had been starving himself. Furthermore, he had fallen madly in love with [character], who rejected his advances. In a a fit of rage or madness, we cannot know, [character] killed himself and sent the letter to you. It seems [character] has been vindicated, and [character] was insane.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Joke's On You

options.text: I blame only myself.

events.text: You should have known better than to trust a fool. [character]'s clumsy attempts to alleviate your illness lead only to more suffering. Your death is long and painful, and it takes the servants several days afterwards to clean up the mess.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Late Night Theology

options.text: If [religion] is this important to you, [character], we should share it together.
[character], you have clearly been duped by this charlatan.

events.text: Hours of accusations, outrage, and theological asides later, you address the pair.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Late Night Theology

options.text: I cannot approve of [religion], but I will not stand in its way, even here.
[character], you have been led astray. I shall see to your salvation.

events.text: Hours of accusations, outrage, and theological asides later, you address the pair.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Left for Dead

options.text: I will take this secret to my grave.

events.text: After receiving a severe beating, you manage to escape your former companions and flee into the night. Several days later, you arrive in [city], where you are nursed back to health and elevated to the throne. You speak of your ordeal to no one.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Let Sleeping Rulers Lie

options.text: A good night’s rest is very important!

events.text: You finally awaken on your own, feeling rested and refreshed. Eventually it occurs to you to enquire about last night’s commotion. As it turns out, the flood wasn’t quite as bad as predicted, serving only to drown the unidentified invaders in their secure camp shortly after they settled down for the night, and put out most of the fire before much damage could be done. Had you not stayed in bed things could have gone very badly indeed!

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Let Sleeping Rulers Lie

options.text: You drift back into a well-deserved slumber.

events.text: Once again your rest is disturbed by a frantic advisor thundering into your chambers. This time they are making a huge fuss about a massive fire engulfing the city. You are too drowsy to really pay attention, but you gather they want the city guard to tear down a vast swath of buildings to prevent the fire from spreading. Quite vexed now, you shout that the next person to disturb your sleep will be skinned alive.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Let Sleeping Rulers Lie

options.text: Return to sleep.

events.text: It seems as if you’ve barely shut your eyes again when another advisor bursts in screaming annoyingly about an unknown invasion force appearing without warning. They want you to rally the army and launch an attack before they can fortify their position, but honestly, you are very cosy where you are and it seems like a lot of effort. You threaten them with dire consequences until they leave.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Lively Banter

options.text: Fine, I'll take the wager. [city] is my ante. May the most glorious nation win!
Ask me again when you aren't too drunk to tell the fountain from a chamber pot.

events.text: Celebrations have gone into the wee hours of the dawn, with [character] and [character] your drinking companions throughout. Voices are raised as you debate the range of [rival] bowmen versus [rival] archers. "I will wager the entire damned city of [city] if my archers cannot outfire yours!"

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Lost in the Labyrinth

options.text: The harrowing experience leaves you changed.

events.text: You enter the imposing Labyrinth and quickly become hopelessly lost inside. Days later, a rescue party finally discovers you.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Loyalty Rewarded

options.text: These men have earned a place of honor.

events.text: As [character] advances, you call to your loyal guards, who quickly snap to attention. Within moments, the Governor of [city] is dead, the victim of numerous mortal wounds. You have managed to escape death this time, but it will most certainly come for you again.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Master of the Labyrinth

options.text: Spread news of your accomplishment far and wide.

events.text: You enter the imposing Labyrinth but keep your wits about you. Using Wisdom, you emerge just before the sun sets to an adoring crowd.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Memorable Performance

options.text: I refuse. He was the better rider.
I will accept the gift graciously.

events.text: You give a memorable performance at the [tribe] contest, but it is no match for [character], whose riding is beyond anything you have ever witnessed. He humbly accepts the prizes, entering the victory circle amid the cheers of his people. As a token of respect, he offers you some of the prize winnings.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Midnight Meeting

options.text: Only the court shall hear of this plot.
The [rival] will pay for this treachery.
Make an attempt to reconcile with [character].

events.text: The guards rush into the garden, surrounding the hapless serving girl. It doesn't take long to find out the truth, that she is an assassin sent by [character] to lure you to your death. It seems that your quick thinking has saved you on this occasion, but what will you do with the knowledge of [character]'s plans?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Monkey Medicine: An improvement

options.text: n/a

events.text: You suddenly feel... better. As if you have improved in some way, but you still feel as sick as ever.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Monkey Medicine: Cured!

options.text: There was no need to fuss.

events.text: On reflection, you really don't feel so bad. In fact, you're now feeling rather foolish about making wishes. It was probably due to your fever, but it seems to have broken.

events.author: Andy Auseon

followsFrom.name: Exploring the Wonders of the World

events.name: Monsoon!

options.text: Leave immediately and return to [city].
Assist the [tribe] guides with their retreat.

requirements.label: Ranger / Pathfinder
tip: The leader must have one of: Ranger; Pathfinder

options.text: We will remain in the wild, where we belong.

events.text: As you reach a distant coast, a sky of majestic black clouds bears down on your expedition. The local [tribe] guides call this easterly storm a "monsoon." Winds toss your caravan, and the lands are soaked in an endless rain. It is time to turn back to [rival], before the weather swamps your entire voyage.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Monumental Evening

options.text: We had a memorable evening.

events.text: Well that speech was far better than I expected. Sacrificing the chicken obviously helped! An evening they will be singing songs about for ever more.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Myth of the Sea Monster

options.text: Pay the men. It is all lies anyway.

events.text: Forty days later, several fishermen come to the court and present several impressive fish. None of the specimens could have swallowed a man whole, let alone kept him alive for three days.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: No Dice

options.text: This game has gone far enough.
I cannot argue with fate.

events.text: [character] impassive stare shifts to a look of satisfaction as the dice land his way. "Summon [character], we would see him return with us."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: No Escape

options.text: My last view was a beautiful one.

events.text: There is no escape. Between the cliffs and [character]'s dagger, you are trapped. Unarmed, you are quickly slain by the Governor of [city], a rival who has suffered your presence long enough.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: No Sign

options.text: Yes, yes, better to know, of course.
Now, if you will kindly get the hell out of my chambers.

events.text: Not a single sprouting, [character], I told you it wasn't likely.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Not So Fresh

options.text: Devote all resources to our recovery.
This demands a fierce response.

events.text: Days after feasting on the delicious [tribe] venison, several members of your extended family begin to feel ill. The royal physician is summoned. Within hours, you, your husband, and your son all show signs of an unnatural illness. There is no denying it. You have been poisoned by [character] and the [tribe].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Nothing Left But Rubble

options.text: They should have expected nothing less for harboring rebels.

events.text: The city holds firm, betraying no sign of [character]. And so, [rival] forces begin delivering the promised retribution.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Odds and Ends

options.text: I cannot refuse such an honor.
I have, ah, just the important task for such a warrior.
Mine to command, you say?

events.text: The dice turn your way, and [character] gives a solemn nod. [character] enters the tent, face weathered and scarred, eyes coldly sizing up his surroundings as if calculating the most efficient order to cut every throat. [character] abruptly stands to leave, "I stand by my word. The strongest of my warriors is yours to command."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: One Wrong Move

options.text: May others learn from my mistake.

events.text: As you and [character] work to balance your delicate humors, the knife slips, and you nick a vital organ. Blood pools quickly on the floor and, despite his best efforts, [character] is unable to staunch the flow. The last thing you see as your essence empties from your body is the blue of a summer's day through the open window.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Only Rubble Remains

options.text: It... it all happened so fast.

events.text: There is a creak, a rumble, and a rush of wind. The mine shaft is gone, and [character] with it.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Only the Best

options.text: I knew it was no good!

events.text: Shortly after the unacceptable wine was taken away there is some kind of commotion with the serving staff. It seems that a number of them decided to sample the rare vintage instead of throwing it out, and have now dropped dead. The wine was poisoned! [character] is very embarrassed by his earlier reaction and begs for you to forgive him.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Our Demands

options.text: We demand money.
We demand wartime resources.
We demand a truce.

events.text: [character], heir to the [rival] throne, has been successfully abducted, and he is now locked in a dungeon of the palace. It is time to talk terms of his release. What shall we demand of [rival]?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Outmaneuvered

options.text: I was, just, uh, admiring the stonework.

events.text: "Comfortable, dear?" You turn abruptly to find [character] behind you, watching you with an unreadable expression.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Over My Dead Body

options.text: We have no choice but victory!

events.text: Barely a day out of the capital, you are stopped on the road by a band of mercenaries. Their leader gleefully informs you of [character] plan: the traitorous heir masterminded this whole thing and has already declared you dead, killed on the road by barbarians. With [rival] leaderless, he has taken his "rightful place" as King [character]. You cannot refute this false claim without getting back to a city. The mercenaries approach. You must survive this fight to return and reclaim the throne!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Over in a Moment

options.text: Long may I reign.

events.text: The duel is short. Brutal. Bloody. And at its end, [character] lies dead. But the crowds cheer. And they go on cheering all the way to the impromptu coronation of [character]. Long live the king.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Overboard!

options.text: I should have suspected him from the start.

events.text: You agree to meet with [character], and the following day you embark on a ship bound for the secret island destination. During the voyage, your retinue is beset by armed attackers, and you are thrown overboard into the thrashing waves. You are determined not to perish alone in the cold sea. Climbing the ship's lines, you aid the crew in repelling the would-be assassins. Only later do you discover the body of their ringleader among the dead: [character].

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Overboard!

options.text: You are enveloped in darkness.

events.text: You agree to meet with [character], and the following day you embark on a ship bound for the secret island destination. During the voyage, your retinue is beset by armed attackers, and you are thrown overboard into the thrashing waves. Before you succumb to the icy embrace of the sea, you glimpse [character] grinning at you from the deck of the ship.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Overtaken

options.text: And so begins the reign of [character].

events.text: Sadly, battlefield leadership has never been your true vocation. Faced with the rage of the charging mercenaries, you panic, attempting to flee the skirmish in a haphazard getaway. You are easily overtaken and slain in the melee.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Picture of Health

options.text: I am as surprised as anyone.

events.text: Your horrifying screams keep the royal house awake through the long night. However, much to everyone's surprise, your outlook improves come the morning. Whatever [character] did with his droppings has rid you of your condition. Perhaps you have misjudged the fool.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Picture of Health

options.text: I am as surprised as anyone.

events.text: Your horrifying screams keep the royal house awake through the long night. However, much to everyone's surprise, your outlook improves come the morning. Whatever [character] did with his droppings has rid you of your condition. Perhaps you have misjudged the fool.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Poor Souls

options.text: Make them comfortable and pray for a full recovery.
Hire healers and doctors from across the Nation.
Put them out of their misery, may the gods forgive me.

events.text: As [character]'s condition worsens, his doctor [character] begins to exhibit the same symptoms. Whispers of curses and plagues fill the palace. Nothing seems to be helping these poor souls.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Pray Tell

options.text: I don't know what you think you are doing here, [character], but you will regret it.
I think we need to talk.

events.text: In the chambers, the muffled sounds resolve into a raised chant. [character] and [character] stand together shoulder to shoulder, enraptured in prayer, until your entrance brings an abrupt and uncertain silence.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Prize Horse

options.text: I have always been lucky.

events.text: Your horse and rider have claimed victory in the grand celebration! It is time to claim your prize!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Ransom

options.text: So be it.
[character] must fend for himself.

events.text: Something has gone wrong in [character] travels, clearly. You receive a brief message in [rival] detailing the sum required for his safe return.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Reaping the Whirlwind

options.text: Sometimes you get the bear, sometimes the bear gets you, and sometimes, the bear just eats everybody.

events.text: Sadly, things did not go according to plan. Yes, [character] met a bad end, but in the confused melee that led to his death, you were also slain by a lucky fool’s blade. Perhaps your heir and [character] will have a better, more peaceful, more prosperous relationship.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Reassurance

options.text: I will send a gift to show my gratitude.
Let us keep our role in this quiet.

events.text: After a tense few weeks of waiting, you receive a message from [character] of the [tribe]. He agrees to your demands, not wanting to anger the mighty forces of [rival]. This is a heartening development. It will be better to have the [tribe] as allies than as enemies.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Recognized!

options.text: This does not look good.
Promise a favor in return for your life.
This will be a thrashing they will not soon forget.
Bow before them, for a [title] is nothing without his subjects.
Convince one of them to betray the others.

events.text: Your fellow explorers do not appreciate your arrogance. They gather around you, daggers drawn. "I thought I recognized him," one man says. "It is the heir to the throne himself. Such a captive would be worth a king's bounty." You prepare for the worst.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Request Refused

options.text: Plead for [character] to reconsider.
Warn [character] that he is making a mistake.
Perhaps some gold will change his mind.

events.text: Offended by our audacity, [character] outright refuses your request to expel all [rival] from his tribe. "We shall keep whatever company we desire," declares the message, ending abruptly. Additional scouts report heightened movement around the [tribe] encampments, but we have no further information.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Resource Drain

options.text: Then we will wait... but not forever.

events.text: [character] is furious at our demands for resources from his already struggling storehouses. However, we have made it very clear that this is the only way to recover his heir alive and unharmed. He will need time to deliberate on this decision.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Restored

options.text: Yes, release [character].
Return him to prison, but shorten the sentence.
He will die in a cell, alone.

events.text: A pair of city guards accompanies a bound [character] on a short expedition outside the walls of [city]. The sun shines brilliantly in a bright blue sky. The wind smells of spring. [character] appears to be a man restored. With this report, the court wonders whether it is time to show the prisoner mercy.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Sacrilege

options.text: Execute those involved, to give the [tribe] justice.
The [tribe] are fortunate we do not dominate them utterly.
The ruins were not marked, and it was a mistake.

events.text: During your leisure voyage, a group of servants in the royal caravan disturb [tribe] site, angering the local tribes. Our people smash stone henges, carve over ancient etchings, and steal anything they perceive as valuable. The [tribe] demand a response from you.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Shadow of Death

options.text: This too shall pass.

events.text: In the last few days, both [character] and [character] have died from the dreadful sickness that appears to have no remedy. You wonder if you could have made wiser choices... as you feel a tickle in your throat, a throbbing in your head.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Sign of Respect

options.text: This was a worthy ride.

events.text: After your performance at the [tribe] horse trials, there is no question of the winner. The crowds cheer your victory, and the other riders humbly salute you. As you take your place in the victory circle, [character] bows. It seems you have earned his respect.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Silent Screams

options.text: This is a bad way to go.

events.text: Your grieving family surrounds you, watching as the priests prepare your body for the afterlife. Summoning all of your strength, you attempt to signal the onlookers to show that, despite your deathly appearance, you are in fact still alive. But even this small movement proves too taxing. As mourners file past your burial party, you glimpse your [tribe] cook flash a knowing smile. Moments later, the priests lower you into the grave and cover you with earth, blotting the light of the sun. Your silent screams will forever go unheard.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Silphium Taken

options.text: Why did I even expect otherwise from some [character] flight of fancy?

events.text: [character] has the silphium delivered within the next days, and at first you consider the matter dealt with. In a matter of months, however, it becomes clear the course of pregnancy is unaltered.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Silphium Taken

options.text: I don't care if [character] was part of some plot or in earnest. I will not suffer to see her face in court again.

events.text: [character] has the silphium delivered within the next days... but while you are no longer with child, the complications linger on.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Silphium Taken

options.text: I suppose there would have been gritting of teeth either way.
[character] really does seem to be on to something here. I should see if greater quantities can be imported.

events.text: [character] has the silphium delivered within the next days, and, smug though she is about it, you have to admit it did what was promised.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Silver Tongue

options.text: I should be more careful next time.

events.text: Your skills at cunning and deceit bear fruit once again, as the crone listens intently to your tale of tragedy. You portray [character]'s death in gruesome detail, describing every heartbreaking detail until the crone is awash in a pool of tears. Begging your apologies, and wishing you better fortunes in the future, the crone departs the palace empty handed.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Sobering Up

options.text: My word is my word.
All is fair in love and war, so I suppose this is war.

events.text: The [rival] archers prove superior. [character] turns to you smugly.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Sobering Up

options.text: Your honor is unimpeachable.

events.text: The [rival] archers prove superior, as you knew they would. [character] hangs his head, and over protests from [character] says, "Well, I am a man of my word. [city] is yours."

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Some Time Later

options.text: What a nice man!

events.text: As you complete the sacrifice, a strange old man whom you had not noticed before suddenly steps forward with a cry of joy. “Oh happy days,” he exclaims! “Your life shall be blessed from this day until your death!” The man smiles warmly at you before striding off, and the positive feeling that his words caused remain with you throughout the day.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Some Time Later

options.text: What a good-looking man. Very charming!

events.text: As you complete the sacrifice, a strange old man whom you had not noticed before suddenly steps forward. “I have some advice for you,” he says, striking a dramatic pose. “Stand tall, and always try to use people’s names, [character]! Make a little effort to know people and they will love you for it” The man winks roguishly at you before striding off, leaving you to ponder his words.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Some Time Later

options.text: Worrisome.

events.text: As you complete the sacrifice, a strange old man whom you had not noticed before suddenly steps forward with a wail of dismay. “You have doomed us with this folly,” he cries! “Your life shall be cursed from this day until your death!” Your guards quickly escort this lunatic away, but you cannot shake the ominous feeling that his words caused.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Some Time Later

options.text: How strange, I didn’t see him waiting.

events.text: As you complete the sacrifice, a strange old man whom you had not noticed before suddenly steps forward. “I have waited a long time to tell you this,” he says, sternly, “but being able to wait patiently for the perfect moment is the key to victory.” The man nods regally before marching off, leaving you to ponder his words.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Some Time Later

options.text: A surprise, to be sure, but a welcome one!

events.text: As you complete the sacrifice, a strange old man whom you had not noticed before suddenly steps forward. “A few coins, wisely invested,” he says, handing you a heavy sack, “can result in you being able to hand a sack of jewels to your inheritor.” Thoroughly distracted by the wealth in your hands, you do not notice the old man leaving.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Some Time Later

options.text: What a nice man!

events.text: As you complete the sacrifice, a strange old man whom you had not noticed before suddenly steps forward. “I have some advice for you,” he says, stroking his beard. “Balance self-interest with the collective good, and seek understanding for its own sake” The man smiles knowingly at you before walking away, and you realise that you feel wiser for his words.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Spolia Opima

options.text: Charge [character], knocking him off the cliffside.
Stick close to [character], so [character] doesn't have a clean shot.
Honestly, this is a bit much.

events.text: Mountains loom over the narrow road where [character] stands, a sheer precipice above and below him. Your heart pounds with the thrill of battle. Arrows zip from behind you. One punches through your armor, lodging in your shoulder. Agony rocks you as you turn and face the bowman; [character] draws another arrow. "Sorry it had to be this way. You should have done what I wanted."

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Spolia Opima

options.text: Victory!

events.text: Scrub land rolls towards the horizon. You beat your sword against your shield and bounce from foot to foot, thirsting for battle. [character] approaches on foot, a gleaming horsehair plume waves from his open helmet in the breeze. Rushing towards him, you narrowly dodge a thrown spear and close the distance. [character] goes wide eyed when your sword slices into his open helmet.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Spolia Opima

options.text: Draw your sword and fight through the pain!

requirements.label: Seven Sins / Insane
tip: The leader must have one of: Seven Sins (a character trait); Insane

options.text: Focus on the pain and charge [character] with dissolute fury.
Mommy...

events.text: The desert sun beats down mercilessly, slowly cooking you in your armor; [character] strides towards you, armor gleaming. With a shout he charges and hurls a spear at you. The spear arcs through the sky and punches through your shield, skewing your arm. Pain blazes through you as blood seeps from the wounded, useless arm. Fear and panic slow your movements.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Spolia Opima

options.text: Bandage and stuff the wound with yarrow.
Stitch the wounds to stop the bleeding.
No! Please no! Don't die! Don't...

events.text: Frosty winds blow, chilling you to the bone. Holding your shield in a death grip, you stamp your feet to stave off the cold. [character] trudges towards you through the snow - poor sod almost looks as miserable as you feel. The fighting warms you and sets you into a steady rhythm, thrusting towards [character], blocking attacks with your shield, parrying blows then counterattacking. Disaster strikes as you slip and crash into the ground. [character] dives towards you delivering the coup de grâce, but in a blur of fur and fury your dog attacks and kills [character]. Your furry friend crawls to you, whimpering, a bloody sword embedded in his trembling flank.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Spolia Opima

options.text: The water is my advantage.
Steady stance! Forward one step at a time!
Attack once more?

events.text: Drifting fog obscures the land, as you eye [character] across a narrow stream. Sweating in your armor, you dismount and splash through the stream towards [character]. He waits just beyond the water with a bared sword. You charge through the stream but are driven back into the muddy waters. Bleeding, soaked, and confused, you desperately seek a solution. What is to be done?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Spolia Opima Defeat

tip: As leader: +5% Unit Trait Modifier / Infantry
As general: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Infantry

options.text: No! We will not!
We will accept the truce.

events.text: [character] comes to you, carrying the body of [character], and sets him before you. Pain fills you at the sight; the memories and wounds of the fight are fresh. "He fought well and died with honor," [character] says, through the pain of his wounds. "Will you honor our agreement?"

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Spolia Opima Victory

options.text: Take his helmet and armor back to the capital.
Send the body and armor back to his family.
Impale the corpse upon a spike, and leave it to rot.

events.text: The body of [character] lies before you. Pain fills you. The memories and wounds of the fight are fresh and bloody. [character] of [rival] comes to you, stunned and holding back tears. "I shall honor our agreement, I ask only that you return his body." What shall we do?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Stunning Blows

options.text: Enemies are everywhere.

events.text: Trained in combat, you evade [character]'s strike easily and counter with a series of stunning blows. He struggles to regain the advantage, but is soon killed by guards in your royal retinue. You must be more careful.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You die!

options.text: Everything is going dark...

events.text: While you survived the first assault, you are soon struck again in the head and collapse to the ground.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You die!

options.text: Everything is going dark...

events.text: Suddenly your throat locks up and you are doubled over by an agonizing pain in your guts. You claw at your throat, but you cannot draw a breath. Your lungs burn and your vision clouds over as you fall to the floor.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You die!

options.text: Everything is going dark...

events.text: An arrow slams into your neck! Your body instantly goes numb as you collapse like a ragdoll. Your last sight is a geyser of blood spurting across your vision.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You die!

options.text: Everything is going dark...

events.text: You jerk your leg away in a panic, but not fast enough. A searing pain flares in your thigh as fangs pierce your flesh. You leap out of bed and stare at the wound in horror, your skin already turning black as your limb swells and you fall to the ground.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You die!

options.text: Everything is going dark...

events.text: Unfortunately you react too slowly to dodge. The knife slams into your chest and you feel yourself falling.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You die!

options.text: Everything is going dark...

events.text: There is no time to react. The cord tightens against your throat and you are pulled backwards with savage strength. Your hands vainly scrabble at your neck, but there is no space to grip the cord and before long there is no strength left in your body.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You survive!

options.text: A close one!

events.text: Your attacker seems surprised that you are still on your feet. He raises his club to strike again, but before he can land another blow, you unsheathe your dagger and cut his throat. Gagging on his own blood, he collapses to the floor. After collecting yourself, you look down at the blood-spattered face of your would-be assassin, and reflect on how court politics came to such a state. What unbridled ambition or fit of madness could have driven someone to this?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You survive!

options.text: That was a close one!

events.text: Your stomach suddenly cramps painfully and you begin to gag. You lurch to a nearby vase and vomit explosively. As quickly as they began, your cramps cease. You wipe your mouth and wonder what could have been added to your wine.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You survive!

options.text: That was a close one!

events.text: An arrow slams into a nearby tree, having missed you by inches! You swing your head, searching for the source of the attack, and catch a glimpse of a hooded figure sprinting away on the roof of a distant building.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You survive!

options.text: A close one!

events.text: With a composed and brave battle cry, which only the most unkind critics would describe as a panicked scream, you leap out of bed. Shortly afterwards, a snake pokes its head out from under your blanket. Somehow you can tell it looks very annoyed.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You survive!

options.text: A close one!

events.text: At the last instant you twist to the side! Your attacker stumbles, off balance, giving you ample time to draw your own dagger and thrust it into his neck before he can recover.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Surprise Attack: You survive!

options.text: A close one!

events.text: Reacting quickly, you manage to get your hands under the cord before it can tighten against your throat. You pull with all your might and hear a startled squawk as your attacker is pulled through the unsuspected hatch in the wall. The assassin hits the floor with a loud crack and lies there unmoving.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Taking Command

options.text: At least it was quick.

events.text: The widespread mutiny begins to falter, as loyal soldiers rise up to defend [rival] against the traitors. As fighting nears the palace, [character] suddenly draws his sword and attacks you. He has been behind the whole affair. You take the blow directly in the heart. Gasping and bleeding, you fall to your knees on the steps of the court you once ruled. [character] stands over you, triumphant.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Talking Him Down

options.text: I must watch my rivals more closely.

events.text: As [character] advances, you notice the dullness of the blade, the sweat on its wielder's brow. He is not a killer. You appeal to [character]'s decency and humanity, remind him of the glory of [rival]. He must not do this! Lowering the dagger, he steps away, only to be tackled by your guards and placed under arrest.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Tense Meeting

options.text: Convince him that you can work together.
Flatter him with promises of royal influence.
Describe the reckoning that will come if he continues.
I have nothing to say to [character].

events.text: Representatives for [character] meet your retinue at the gates of [city], and they take you to meet with him. The meeting is cordial, but an air of tension fills the chamber. "This city no longer obeys the throne in [city]. You must relinquish your grip or suffer the consequences."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Aftermath

options.text: [character] seemed to enjoy it at least.

events.text: Ministers shake their heads at the costs of the festivity's architectural damage alone.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Barley Sprouts

options.text: You know, I think that might be for the best.
No, thank you. We will see what the heavens will.

events.text: This level of sprouting is, supposedly, clear. You are with child. [character] is practically buzzing with the opportunity to continue bestowing wisdom, "You know dear, I do know just the thing if you are... uncertain about going through with this. Silphium, wonderful plant, cures all kinds of problems, though a bit challenging to get hold of. Shall I see if some can be arranged?"

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Bloody Court

options.text: I wish to focus only on ruling justly.
Let them sing of me and compose epic verse.
Scrub all mentions of [character] from history.

events.text: After dispatching his bodyguards with ease, you slay [character] in front of the court. Raising your sullied blade in one hand and [character]'s head in the other, you roar "Behold! The terrible price of treason." In response to the failed coup, the government renews its pledge of loyalty. How do you wish this moment to be remembered?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Case of the Horse

options.text: It is too late now. Surrender the city.
I feel Foolish, but we will fight to the death!

events.text: While we slept after the celebration of our victory, enemy [rival] units crawled out of the wooden horse that we brought inside our Walls and started attacking our citizens. The enemy is inside the city! What would you have us do?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The Case of the Horse

options.text: Glue the wood together and let them weaken in starvation.
Let us imprison them and work them for free.
I knew that already; we are heating the oil to pour on them as we speak!

events.text: The citizens of [city] are quite cheered by the celebrations, but they feel that the horse might have hidden [rival] soldiers sealed inside it. What would you have us do?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Claimant Arrives

options.text: Placate him with control of [city].
[character] will not rule even a single field of [rival].

events.text: Reaching the outskirts of [city], [character] demands rule over the land he believes he is entitled to.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Claimant Arrives

options.text: Placate him with control of [city].
[character] will not rule even a single field of [rival].

events.text: Reaching the outskirts of [city], [character] demands rule over the land he believes he is entitled to.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Forgotten Prophet

options.text: Send a messenger to ask [character] for information.
Search for someone within your nation who can translate the fragment.
Send the tablet back to [rival] as a gift.

events.text: Consulting with various scholars and searching through the palace's library proves fruitless. It is as if the prophet never existed. It is not until weeks later that a chance encounter reminds you of the quest, when a visiting merchant offers you a rare find, a stone tablet unearthed from a ruined temple and decorated with the same story that you encountered in your research. The pictures are surrounded by writing in an archaic form of. Pressing the merchant further, reveals that it is a common story in [rival], although in their version the hero is an ancestor of [character], and a [religion], rather than [religion] prophet.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Gods do not Play Dice

options.text: I think I shall have to see about those dice tables [character] is always talking about.
Having bested the Gods themselves, I think I'd best quit while I'm ahead.

events.text: Perhaps the Gods favor you. Perhaps the priestesses are charlatans and liars. Perhaps powers of prognostication are dulled by being woken in the middle of the night to entertain the [title] of [rival]. Regardless, the night's winnings are certainly the cherry on top of an excellent evening.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Heir's Journey

options.text: This ordeal made me stronger.

events.text: Sneaking away after dark, you avoid roads and busy areas, knowing that many in [rival] may be on the lookout for the heir, and not with good intentions. After a week's trek through the wilderness, you emerge in the outskirts of [city]. Servants at the palace rejoice when they see you and take you into their care. Rested and healthy, you ascend the throne of [rival]. At last.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Last Laugh

options.text: Trust no one.

events.text: It is no use. Shadows fall across your chambers, and your dreams are split by terror and misery. When morning comes, you cannot move, cannot see, cannot cry out. You hear the sweet, cruel laughter of [character] as he comes to collect your crown.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Last One Standing

options.text: Admit everything and beg to be released.
Refuse to plead.

events.text: [character] is relentless, his strikes coming heavy and fast. After each blow he shouts the name of his father, "[character]! [character]! [character]!" Under such a furious attack there is no room for tactics or skillful fighting. The sheer force of anger beats you back until your foot slips in the mud and rain and you crash to the floor. [character] looks down on you, and offers mercy if you are willing to admit your wrongs and beg for your life.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Last One Standing

options.text: That is one less enemy to worry about.

events.text: [character] steps forward to fight, the last step he ever takes. The warriors that came with him cry out in horror as your guards' arrows thud into his chest, knocking him to the floor. Your guards quickly hunt down and kill [character] companions, leaving them on the road arranged as if killed by thieves. You won't make the same mistake twice: No one will be coming to avenge [character].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Last One Standing

options.text: No, [character] is too dangerous to be left alive.
Allow [character] to walk free.

events.text: The fight is short but tense, blades clashing as you both struggle to keep your footing in the mud and rain. Then [character] misses a heavy swing and it is over. A well placed strike fully overbalances him and your opponent crashes heavily to the ground. Victory is yours, will you show mercy?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: The Leviathan's Doom

options.text: It is done.

events.text: Forty days later, several fishermen come to the court and offer you a pair of radiant eggs, which shimmer and glow in the sunlight. You have them placed in the treasury. That night a terrible roar awakens you, smoke and fire fill the streets of [city]. Has the Leviathan followed the fishermen, to take its revenge? A night of chaos follows as you join your guard in trying to contain the fires and many lives are lost. Wild rumors circulate about a great beast roaming the streets, crushing buildings and consuming citizens, but try as you might you can never catch a glimpse of it yourself. Perhaps the creature was driven off, or perhaps it was only the product of panicked minds, but in either case it is wise to assure the people of [city] that you have slain the beast and they need fear it no more.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Long Night

options.text: Banish the boy and his fool.
Execute them!
[character] may one day be useful.

events.text: You experience a slumber unlike any other - riven by screams and nightmares - but by morning you feel free of torment. You have survived poisoning at the hands of [character] and his minion. What shall you have us do in retribution?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Loser

options.text: Maybe next time.

tip: As leader: +50 Unit Trait XP / Mounted
As governor: +100 Unit Trait XP / Mounted

options.text: If only I had riden myself!

events.text: Your horse and rider have failed to claim victory at the grand celebration. At least the wager will go to a good cause.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The More the Merrier

options.text: This is just getting started.
Time to take my leave.

events.text: [character] reputation as the life of a party is not unearned. As the evening proceeds there is a direct and inverse relationship between quantity of wine and amount of clothing worn. A distractingly naked makes to refill your cup.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Next Morning

options.text: What a wonderful night!

events.text: The morning after a great royal feast, you wake up next to one of your minor courtiers. The affair was short... but entertaining. Much of the night was spent in deep conversation with your paramour, talking about everything from the construction of palaces to your favorite desserts.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Next Morning

options.text: What a wonderful night!

events.text: The morning after a great royal feast, you wake up next to one of your minor courtiers. The affair was short... but entertaining. The short time that you had together was exactly what you needed. Returning to your duties you feel ready to conquer anything.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Next Morning

options.text: Curses upon them all!

events.text: The morning after a great royal feast, you wake up next to one of your minor courtiers. The affair was short... but entertaining. The problems start the next day, when news of your exploits starts to travel around the court. The night was fun, but you can't shake off a feeling that you are being laughed at behind your back.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Path to Redemption

options.text: The path to redemption is long but valuable.

events.text: You are approached by, the same that received [character] confession. He tells you that the [religion] clergy are sure that [character] found peace and redemption for the many, many sins that he shared in such richly descriptive language and such painfully intricate detail. This will undoubtedly reflect well on your own rule.

events.name: The Path to Redemption

options.text: The path to redemption is long but valuable.

events.text: You are approached by, the same that received [character] confession. He tells you that the [religion] clergy are sure that [character] found peace and redemption for even the darkest sins that he shared so openly and honestly. This will undoubtedly reflect well on your own rule.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Path to Redemption

options.text: Invite [character] to dine with you as a friend.
Find evidence that [character] attacked the clergy.
Ignore the slander.
Condemn [character] attempts to slander one forgiven in the eyes of.

events.text: The first warning of trouble is when you are approached by some of the [religion] leaders, worried that had gone missing. Soon after, you hear that [character] has started spreading rumors across [city] about the various sins of [character], claiming that he confessed to them before passing away. Such claims are an attempt to undermine your authority and tarnish the dynasty's reputation. How will you deal with this unscrupulous rival?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Pipes are Calling

options.text: Lovely idea. Don't let me disturb you.
Honestly, you can hear that from here to [city]. Just get rid of the damned thing.

events.text: As you enter, [character] looks up sheepishly from the tangle of cloth and wooden pipes he was blowing into. The discordant groan ceases, and after an awkward moment he offers, "Apologies, I didn't realize it would be so loud. These ney-anban were a gift, and I thought it might be a quiet moment to practice..."

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: The Prophet Strikes Back

options.text: We must be careful of this firebrand.
We cannot condone this. [character] must be exiled.
That is enough. Guards, kill [character].

events.text: That day, four hundred and fifty acolytes call upon the old gods to light their sacrifice on fire and break the drought. The priests flog themselves with spears and whips, blood covers the ground around the altar, as they scream and dance for their gods. "Oy fellas! Maybe your gods are meditating or maybe they're asleep, yeah?" [character] taunts the priests incessantly. "I mean they do love a good orgy... Oh! What if they're on a journey?" When the evening arrives, [character] takes twelve stones, builds a humble altar, digs a trench around the altar. He slaughters his bull upon the altar and orders twelve barrels of precious water poured over the altar, soaking the very stones. "Hear me, O Jehovah, that this people may know that you are God," begs [character] in solemn prayer as Fire from heaven strikes the altar and consumes the bull, wood, stones, and water in the trench. "Seize these false priests!" [character] bellows to the crowd, driving them into a frenzy. That night [character] kills each of the acolytes and, a few days later, rain returns.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Prophet's Cave

options.text: Drink from the spring.
Open the cave as a site of pilgrimage.
Destroy the cave.

events.text: Your newfound helper points the way to the prophet's cave as promised. It is a humble place, carved into a cliff near the border of [rival] with a small spring at the back creating a small stream that winds out along the stone floor. The walls are covered with and writings, praising the glory of and telling the prophet's full story. They say that this is where the prophet's journey started after drinking from the water and being found worthy by. The writings predict that a [title] will one day arrive who will have to decide, to drink and be tested or to share the sacred waters with the world. And now you are here. The [rival] are unlikely to take kindly to you revealing the story they have been trying to erase, but this is an undoubtedly holy site for [religion].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Streets of [city]

options.text: Out of curiosity, how do the local [rival] say 'no biting'?

events.text: The bazaars of [city] are brimming with an overwhelming abundance of goods, smells, and packs of street dogs. New supplies for further exploration are secured, while a passing kindness to a friendly mutt earns [character] an unshakable companion.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Tournament at [city]

options.text: People will be talking about this fight for years to come.

events.text: Although the fight is long and tense, at the end it is your favored [family] champion who is defeated, falling at the feet of the overwhelming [family]. Although put out that their [family] champion lost, the crowd still celebrate such a spectacle of a fight. The warrior waves to and salutes you, drawing further cheers and cries of praise from the adoring masses.

events.text: Although the fight is long and tense, in the end it is your favored [family] champion who stands victorious. Drinking in the adulation of the crowd, the fighter waves to and salutes you, drawing further cheers and cries of praise from the adoring masses.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Trail of Heroes

options.text: You push the horses to ride faster than before.
You jump to action before there is a chance to think.
Charge!
It escapes you this time. Legends are not easy prey!

events.text: You track the creature for a number of days, assisted by the [unit] who reported the sighting. At last the cry goes out, "There it is!" All you see is a blurred shadow as the creature flees back into the woods. It's getting away!

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Voyage Ruse

options.text: I will deal with him eventually.
Give him time to reflect on his treachery.
Make efforts to earn [character]'s trust.

events.text: With some quickly dispatched messengers, you learn that [character] has not agreed to any secret meeting. The council with [rival] was simply a ruse to get you alone, far from your usual safeguards. We suspect that [character] is behind this plot, and that he will stop at nothing to see your reign ended.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Through the Fire
events.text: [character] guides you through the stages of the ritual, grinding down a series of herbs that you do not recognize into a thick paste. The sludge-like mixture is sour on your tongue, but there is little time for such thoughts - visions of the lands of the dead fill your senses and you fall before Pluton and ask the god to allow you to take [character] place. In your dreams, Pluton is moved by your sacrifice and decrees that you can both leave. When you wake [character] is sitting by your bed, the picture of perfect health.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Through the Fire

options.text: Berate [character] for almost costing you your life.

events.text: [character] guides the servant through the stages of the ritual, grinding down a series of herbs that you do not recognize into a thick paste. The sludge-like mixture is thick on the tongue, but there is little time for such thoughts - the servant collapses to the floor in convulsions. By the day's end, it is clear that the servant is not going to wake and there is no change to [character] condition.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Traitorous Monkey

options.text: Never trust an adorable court monkey!

events.text: Lying in bed, you hear the pitter patter of tiny feet... and it is terrifying. The last thing you feel is a set of sharp teeth sinking into your neck. Somehow, [character] has turned our adorable court monkey assassin against you.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Triple Cross!

options.text: Well that didn’t go according to plan…

events.text: Unfortunately, nothing was as it seemed. All of your reports were false. It was a ruse by [character] and his heir, [character], designed to draw you out and expose you. Unfortunately, it worked. [character] summoned you at the appointed hour when the deed was to be done, and that’s when you discovered that you were the intended victim. Sadly, your reign ends here, and now, your nation will be plunged into war with a new and untested leader…

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Ultimatum

options.text: I cannot part with my treasures! Let them have [character]!
Such an offer is insulting. I value nothing more than [character].
How about a drinking contest? Winner take all!
I will help them improve their methods of coercion.

events.text: As you and your husband enjoy the views on the outskirts of [rival], your caravan is set upon by a gang of raiders. The ruffians round up your servants, taking full inventory of the goods you brought with you on the voyage. "Your husband will fetch a fine price on the market," says the gang's leader. "I will make you a deal. Give us this handsome man, and we will let the rest of you go."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Unchallenged

options.text: It is good to be home.

events.text: Realizing that they have underestimated you, your former companions drop their weapons and step away. The new [title] of [rival] is not to be challenged. In fact, when only moments ago they brandished weapons, now they bow before you. You return to [city] and ascend the throne.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Under Arrest

options.text: Threaten him with grievous harm.
Recognize his sham trial.
Say nothing. Do not dignify this with a response.

events.text: Arriving in [city], the court's emissaries find a local government locked in the tyrannical grip of [character]. They are immediately placed under arrest, accused of attempting to destabilize the running of the city. [character] promises a showy trial.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Unexpected Visit: You die!

options.text: Everything is going dark...

events.text: You are able to dodge the first swing, but [character] skilfully reverses course and his backswing smashes the blade into your chest. You are thrown to the floor. “[character]... Why?” you gasp, but you do not hear any answer.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Unexpected Visit: You survive!

options.text: A close one!

events.text: You are able to dodge the first swing, and while [character] is off balance you catch him in a grapple. [character], unwilling to let go of the axe but unable to swing it in such close quarters, is at a disadvantage and you throw him to the floor. He lands poorly, his head impacting on the hard ground with a loud crack. He does not rise again.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Unhappy Raiders

options.text: Next time, I will stay closer to home.

events.text: Despite your best efforts, the ragged highwaymen remain unswayed. They plunder your traveling caravan, stealing goods and terrorizing servants. Before he departs, the gang's leader cuts your cheek with his rusty dagger. "A little gift to remember me by," he shouts, as he rides into the shadows.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Unimpressed

options.text: That went badly.

events.text: Unimpressed, the Mercenary draw their weapons and make short work of your personal guards. "You should have agreed to our demands," says one of the outlaws, as he twists the dagger in your belly. They recover the goods, set fire to your tent, and leave you and your men dying in the dirt.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Unviable

options.text: Let [character] wallow in his self-pity.
I wish to help support this sad, mad woman.
Tell [character] to remove this thorn from my side.

events.text: After consulting the calendars for the past year, your royal doctors have found that you cannot be the father of [character]'s child. She is lying to retain her grip on courtly influence. But now the truth is out.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Unwelcome

options.text: [character] is the next ruler's problem now.

events.text: As your retinue enters [city], Governor [character]'s forces converge on the city gates. They surround you, weapons drawn. The treasonous [character] emerges. "You have done yourself a great disservice coming here. You wield no power in [city]."

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Victorious Monkey

options.text: My plan is working perfectly.

events.text: It is done. Our adorable court monkey, now assassin, has successfully murdered [character]. Luckily, nobody knows that you are responsible.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Victory at the Games

options.text: Alas!

events.text: [character] ran to victory and brought much honor upon your house in the games. Unfortunately the young prodigy was waylaid by some of the other competitors returning to [city] in shame. [character] was killed in the fight.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Vision from Beyond

options.text: To honor and raise up our ancestors.
To search for truth in every endeavor.
To adhere to the strict laws of faith.
I will choose my goals when the time is right.

events.text: The following evening, you lie in wait, ready for the arrival of the phantom [character]. He appears pleased that you have shed your fear. "I mean you no harm," he says in a hollow whisper. "I come to show you a vision from beyond." [character] proceeds to describe the [rival] that he can see on the horizon, a nation of great wisdom and prosperity, one that will stand eternal. To achieve this legacy, he advises you to pursue one of the following goals.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Vision from Beyond

options.text: The dead, I think, can care for themselves.

events.text: You must have fallen asleep, even in your preparedness. The words of a dream drain from your mind, even as you reach for them. There is a feeling of comfort that lingers, though, and perhaps the face of [character]?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Walk Away

options.text: I reminded them of their place.

events.text: Realizing that they are in the presence of someone with great authority and influence, the Mercenary rescind their demands. They will be happy to keep their lives. You let them go, with warnings to not set foot in your lands again.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Wandering the Wilderness

options.text: I will strive to learn from my mistakes.

events.text: Within minutes of escaping your camp, you realize that your navigational skills are profoundly lacking. Lost beneath a sky full of stars, you wander the wilderness. Days pass. You thirst and hunger with no relief. Later, a caravan of merchants discovers you half-mad in a ditch and nurses you back to health. By the time you finally reach [city], you have suffered an ordeal that would have broken a lesser man.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Wild Revels

options.text: Kill any who saw me.
How embarrassing...

events.text: The guards don't have to look long to find your clothes, which are jauntily adorning a statue right in the center of [city]. Asked how they got there, the locals laughingly tell of how you stumbled across the city in the night, making barely coherent drunken speeches, before stripping and clothing the statue after commenting that it looked cold.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Wild Revels

options.text: A companion will make these revels even more enjoyable!
Do your worst.

events.text: Your guards fail to find your clothes, although a few weeks later you spot [character] wearing a distinctly familiar ring. Cornering him to demand an explanation, [character] freely admits to taking your clothes, hoping that the hunt would lead you back to him. "I hope you enjoyed the revelry as much as I did, perhaps this could be a regular occurrence? If not, me and my friends have some fantastic stories to tell that I'm sure would delight the court."

events.name: Wonders Await

options.text: It is time to return home.

events.text: Visiting [rival], you marvel at their engineering feats, including the incomparable Pyramids. You and your caravan are not the only tourists viewing this architectural marvel. People from all over the world have come to see with their own eyes what they had only heard about in stories. You are inspired to bring such spectacle back home to [rival].

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Wrong Turn

options.text: I have [character] to thank for my life.

events.text: Fleeing from the palace, a small retinue follows [character] into a series of secret chambers beneath [city]. The tunnels are ancient and reek of filth and decay. Many of your group end up lost in the darkness. In a moment of confusion, [character] draws his sword and attacks you fiercely. He has been behind the whole mutinous affair. Several of your most loyal guards manage to subdue the traitorous officer, but not before he has killed Chancellor [character].

events.author: Josh Unsworth

followsFrom.name: The One Who Would be King

events.name: [character]

options.text: Execute him in [city], where it started.
Refuse to punish the one that stood against you.

events.text: The news spreads like wildfire - [character] has been captured in a skirmish. People line the streets to watch the procession and to catch a glimpse of the famous rebel, walking behind his captors in chains. The threat of war is over, but it is still to be decided what should be done with the remaining rebels. [character] looks up and behind those eyes you see a lifetime of suffering, of pain and grief beyond that which any person should have to endure.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Surrendered

options.text: [character] shall die for his treason.
[character] shall die for his treason... slowly.
I refuse to make a martyr of [character].

events.text: [character] looks you in the eye as he is brought before you, betrayed by his own people. You ask what he has to say for himself but receive only echoing silence. No pleas of mercy, no last minute negotiations, only stoic resignation.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: [character]'s Revival

options.text: I must be either lucky or chosen.

events.text: Surprising priests and physicians alike, your husband has started to recover from his sickness, proving prognosticators wrong. Sadly, court scientist [character], who has been attending the king, does not fare as well. He dies late one evening, riven with pain and pustules.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [city] Within Reach

options.text: [character] ambition has a certain appeal.
Pure flights of fancy.

events.text: [character] reports on [city] have a breathless tone. The great wealth, exotic delights, and, of course, scant defenses. He is truly convinced a lightning strike could pry the city from the grasp of [rival].
